_comment: REFERENCE ONLY — not a plan file. JSON has no comments, so read stalwart/README.md alongside this. Field names are from the MtaRoute docs; the plan envelope must come from `stalwart-cli snapshot` against a running server, because the CLI is schema-driven and the server is the authority on its own shape.
authUsername: REPLACE — created at SMTP2GO under Sending > SMTP Users

_notes.why_environment_variable: The `Value` variant would inline the password into a file committed to a PUBLIC repo — and deleting a secret from git does not remove it from history. EnvironmentVariable keeps the plan committable and the secret in the vault.
_notes.why_the_name_is_generic: RELAY_SMTP_PASSWORD, not SMTP2GO_PASSWORD. The relay is explicitly a for-now choice, and a provider-shaped name would spread that choice into the compose file, the systemd unit, the .env and the plan — turning a one-object swap into a rename across five places.
_notes.port_choice: 8465, NOT 465, and this is load-bearing. Infomaniak blocks outbound 25 by default and opens it on request; other hosts block some combination of 25, 465 and 587. We never ask, because we never need it. 8465 is SMTP2GO's implicit-TLS port on a number nobody filters, so it keeps the security property of 465 — no cleartext phase for an attacker to strip — while making the relay path independent of the host's port politics. Their TLS ports are 25/587/2525/8025/80 and their SSL ports are 465/8465/443; 2525 is the fallback if 8465 is ever unreachable. Switch to 465 only if you have confirmed egress is open, and never to a STARTTLS port without requiring TLS on the route: a stripped connection would offer these credentials in clear.
_notes.dane_and_mtasts: Both MUST be disabled on this route. They assert properties of direct-to-MX delivery that are false with a smarthost in the path, and the resulting failures present as TLS errors — which sends you debugging certificates instead of routing. The key differs by version; confirm it in your snapshot.
_notes.link_tracking: Turn it OFF at SMTP2GO — Sending > SMTP Users > your user > Tracking & Status, BOTH Click Tracking and Open Tracking. It is a per-user setting, so a second SMTP user created later starts with tracking on again. It rewrites URLs in the message body, and Stalwart signed that body with our DKIM key before handoff — a rewrite after signing invalidates the signature. This is a deduction from how DKIM body hashing works, not something SMTP2GO documents either way, so treat it as a thing to VERIFY at phase 4 rather than a settled fact. It is also simply unwanted: this is correspondence, not marketing.
_notes.second_signature: SMTP2GO adds its own DKIM signature via the CNAME delegated in infra/relay.tf. Two aligned signatures is legal and DMARC passes if either validates. Ours is the one that survives changing relay.
_notes.signed_headers: Sign From:Subject:To and NOTHING ELSE. SMTP2GO rewrites Message-Id and regenerates Date, so signing either produces dkim=fail at the receiver. The Date rewrite is the subtle one - the relay usually stamps the same second the message was signed, so the headers look identical. Stalwart's default set includes both; change it on the DkimSignature, not in DNS, because the published key is unaffected.
_notes.ed25519_at_gmail: Gmail reports dkim=neutral (no key) for RFC 8463 ed25519 signatures. It is a receiver limitation, not a misconfiguration, and neutral does not fail DMARC - the RSA signature carries alignment. Keep both; other receivers do validate ed25519.
